newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU criteria be to strictly applied -- De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU criteria be to strictly applied -- De Silguy.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault De Silguy said on Monday the Maastricht treaty single currency criteria would be rigourously applied when chosing the nations to take part in the project.
"We have to be assured that budgetary consolidation is durable," De Silguy told a presentation of a book on Economic and Monetary Union written by Reuter journalists.
"That is why we will also take into account 1998 budgets that have been adopted," he added, reiterating a decision taken by European Union finance ministers at the weekend.
"We have to take as little risk as possible with the quality of the Euro," he said.

De Silguy declined to comment directly on remarks reportedly made at the weekend by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel that appeared to indicate a softening in Germany's rigid approach to interpreting the Maastricht criteria.
But he told Reuters Financial Television separately: "It is not possible to fudge the figure. It is not possible to soften the conditions."

"The decision (on EMU) will be taken at the end of April or the beginning of May 1998...if we have taken that date it is because we need to know the definitive (economic) figures of 1997," he told the book launch.
"Until I have these figures I am unable to say how the decision will be taken. I don't have a crystal ball," he added.
